newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank says help to state budget limited.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank says help to state budget limited.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Wednesday its participation in helping finance the state budget was limited, and it would only do so to prevent interest rates from rising.

"We have started to participate in state budget financing but only on gradually declining volumes and rather to slow down the (rise) of interbank money market rates," Peter Andresic, NBS chief dealer, told Reuters.
"The current T-bill yield is high, and this suggests the ministry should have no problem refinancing its budget needs at such rate," he added.

The average yield on the Finance Ministry's T-bills, a strong determining factor for interbank money market rates, hit 11.94 percent on Wednesday, up from 11.25 percent in the last auction of similar bills.

The Slovak state budget deficit widened sharply to 13.4 billion crowns for the January-September period from 7.9 billion in the first eight months of 1996, while the full-year deficit projection is 26.95 billion crowns.

Andresic said the NBS has intervened through several seven-day purchases of the ministry's T-bills totalling more than 16 billion crowns in the past two months. "(But) such intervention cannot be characterised as refinancing," he added.
The ministry recently said lower-than-expected tax revenue and increasing expenditures linked to state debt are causing problems in meeting the state budget in the last quarter of 1996.

However, analysts warned that commercial banks appeared to have their investment portfolios filled through the end of the year and may have little interest in non-taxed revenue from the ministry's T-bills.
Slovak banks cover their costs with taxed revenue such as interbank deposits.
